## Permission boundaries

Backend is authority, not visibility alone. `AdminWriteOnly`: channel and regular/custom playlist reads available to authenticated users, writes admin; video detail delete admin. `AdminOnly`: downloads (including reads), task APIs, refresh, operational appsettings/cookie/token/backup/snapshot/membership. App config GET available to authenticated users (`AdminWriteOnly`). User config/account, watched/progress, search and statistics authenticated. Important existing mismatch: frontend `useIsAdmin` checks staff OR superuser; backend `check_admin` checks staff OR membership in `admin` group. Superuser-only and admin-group-only accounts need explicit review; fixtures use staff admin to avoid pretending mismatch is resolved. Confirm ordinary-account mounted screens never issue forbidden operational reads unnecessarily and do not expose admin writes. Test 401 and 403 separately.

ApplicationStats, BiggestChannelsStats, Button, ChannelAutoIgnoreFilter, ChannelBanner, ChannelIcon, ChannelList, ChannelOverview, ChannelRollingWindow, CommentBox, DownloadHistoryStats, DownloadListItem, EmbeddableVideoPlayer, Filterbar, Footer, FormattedNumber, GoogleCast, InputConfig, Linkify, LoadingIndicator, MembershipAppsettings, MoveVideoMenu, Navigation, NavigationItem, Notifications, OverviewStats, Pagination, PaginationDummy, PlaylistList, PlaylistThumbnail, ScrollToTop, SearchExampleQueries, SettingsNavigation, StatsInfoBoxItem, SubtitleList, ToggleConfig, VideoList, VideoListItem, VideoListItemTable, VideoPlayer, VideoThumbail, VideoTypeStats, WatchedCheckBox, WatchProgressStats.

## Required mounted-browser matrix

Admin and ordinary account; desktop/mobile; keyboard and labeled fields; direct deep links and back; success/empty/error/delayed load; mutation success/failure/401/403; persistence after reload; delete confirmation cancel; local action log matching intended request; no horizontal overflow; classic and modern CSS isolation. Native media playback, Google Cast, actual external integrations, Python regex validation, server authorization and real queue scheduling need separate backend/device checks. Fixtures do not prove those behaviors.
